evidence.title: Authors report that multi-principal scheduling agents fail coordination despite individually solvable tasks; communication modality and mixed-model configuration change outcomes.

evidence.limitations: Ten runs per condition and two scheduling scenarios limit generality. Some configurations achieved high success. Proposed social-harness architecture is not an empirically validated general defense; faulty-agent experiments differ from honest-agent failures.
evidence.open_questions: Generality, independent replication or formal validation beyond the inspected scope remain open.

terms.name: Assurance
terms.definition: Evidence-supported confidence that specified properties or outcomes will hold under stated objectives, operating conditions, and assumptions. Assurance has a defined scope and can lose relevance when those conditions change.

terms.name: Cross-system feedback
terms.definition: A pattern in which an action or output from one technical or organizational process affects activity elsewhere and subsequent responses modify conditions for additional participants. Many response paths may exist; there need not be a single linear loop.
